# healthchecksio_checks (Data Source)

The checks of the project, with their status. A read-only API key is sufficient.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "healthchecksio_checks" "prod" {
  tags = ["prod"]
}

output "down" {
  value = [for c in data.healthchecksio_checks.prod.checks : c.name if c.status == "down"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `slug` (String) Give only the checks with this slug.
- `tags` (Set of String) Give only the checks that have all of these tags.

### Read-Only

- `checks` (Attributes List) The checks, in the order of the API. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--checks))

<a id="nestedatt--checks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `checks`

Read-Only:

- `badge_url` (String) The URL of the 2-state SVG badge of the check.
- `channels` (Set of String) The UUIDs of the integrations of the check. Null with a read-only key.
- `desc` (String) The description of the check.
- `failure_kw` (Set of String) The failure keywords.
- `filter_body` (Boolean) Look for the keywords in the body of an email ping.
- `filter_default_fail` (Boolean) A filtered ping that has no keyword is a failure signal.
- `filter_http_body` (Boolean) Look for the keywords in the body of an HTTP ping.
- `filter_subject` (Boolean) Look for the keywords in the subject of an email ping.
- `grace` (Number) The grace period, in seconds.
- `id` (String) The unique_key of the check.
- `last_duration` (Number) The duration of the last job in seconds, from its start signal to its next signal, or null.
- `last_ping` (String) The time of the last ping (RFC 3339), or null.
- `manual_resume` (Boolean) If true, a paused check ignores pings until you resume it.
- `methods` (String) The HTTP methods for pings: "" or "POST".
- `n_pings` (Number) The number of pings that the check got.
- `name` (String) The name of the check.
- `next_ping` (String) The time when the grace period starts (RFC 3339), or null.
- `ping_url` (String, Sensitive) The ping URL. Null with a read-only key.
- `schedule` (String) The cron or OnCalendar expression. Null for a simple check.
- `slug` (String) The slug of the check.
- `start_kw` (Set of String) The start keywords.
- `started` (Boolean) True when the check got a start signal and waits for the next signal.
- `status` (String) The status: new, up, grace, down or paused.
- `success_kw` (Set of String) The success keywords.
- `tags` (Set of String) The tags of the check.
- `timeout` (Number) The period of a simple check, in seconds. Null for a check with a schedule.
- `tz` (String) The time zone of the schedule. Null for a simple check.
- `uuid` (String, Sensitive) The UUID of the check. Null with a read-only key.
